dedupe_keys.name: itu ict statistics world telecommunication ict indicators and datahub

description: The International Telecommunication Union, the UN specialised agency for information and communication technologies, is the official source of global ICT statistics. It collects indicators from national regulators, ministries and statistical offices and publishes them for monitoring digital development and universal connectivity targets. The statistics page offers downloadable time series (Excel, 2005 to 2025) for the world, geographic regions, urban and rural areas and development groups on fixed and mobile telephone subscriptions, fixed and mobile broadband subscriptions, the population covered by mobile-cellular and mobile-broadband networks, internet use by sex, age and area, and mobile phone ownership; aggregates follow ITU regions, least developed, landlocked and small island groups and World Bank income groups. Country-level series are published on the ITU DataHub, alongside ICT Facts and Figures, ICT price baskets, the digital development dashboard, the ICT Development Index and historical statistics from 1849 to 1967. ITU estimated for 2025 that about 6 billion people, 74 per cent of the world's population, use the internet. Access is free through the web pages and downloadable spreadsheets; the DataHub refused scripted and page-fetch access on 26 September 2026, and a reuse licence was not stated on the page read. Caveats: data are reported by countries with differing definitions and gaps, many values are ITU estimates, and coverage indicators describe population coverage, not network geometry. Simulation uses: national and regional context for demand, digital divide and social vulnerability in resilience and capacity-planning studies of telecom networks. Related records: Ookla and M-Lab performance data and OpenCelliD site data.
